title: Scalar compatibility of the actual projective-line adjunction counit
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. All schemes below are separated and finite type over $k$, and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, and choose $N=\ell^n\geq1$ annihilating both. On small ordinary etale sites use constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and $T_T=(-)_B=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Write $D^b_{ctf}$ for bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude, as in [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer], and $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$ for $R=A,B$ [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. For a standing base $S$, set $q:P=\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, $F_R=Rq_{*,R}$ and $G_R=q_R^*(-)\otimes_R^LR_P(1)[2]$. Use the actual adjunction $F_R\dashv G_R$ with counit $\epsilon_R$ and projection-formula normalization of [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction]. Let $\beta_q:T_SF_A\to F_BT_P$ be the fixed proper coefficient map [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. Let $a_K:T_PG_AK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_BT_SK$ be the canonical tensor/pullback, Tate and shift comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Then for every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(S_{et},A)$,
$$\epsilon_{B,T_SK}\,F_B(a_K)\,\beta_q(G_AK)=T_S(\epsilon_{A,K}).$$
In particular $a_K$ is the mate of $\beta_q^{-1}$ on these finite-Tor subcategories.

proof.text: The standing schemes $S$ and $P$ are Noetherian by finite type over the field. Choose a bounded flat constructible model $C$ of $K$ using the input-model theorem; it also gives $X=T_SK\in D^b_{ctf}$. Apply the pullback-line model lemma with $f=q$, $E=A_P(1)$ and $r=2$; the twist is etale locally free of rank one. It gives a bounded K-flat constructible model $(q^{-1}C\otimes A_P(1))[2]$ of $G_AK$ and its Tor interval. The same holds over $B$. Thus the proper coefficient theorem makes $\beta_q(G_AK)$ invertible. The integer $N$ is a unit on these schemes because $\ell\ne p$.

proof.text: Put $L_R=R_P(1)[2]$, $H_R=F_RL_R$, and use the balanced shifted twist comparison $\lambda:T_PL_A\simeq L_B$. Set $b=F_B(\lambda)\beta_q(L_A)$, let $m$ and $e:T_SA_S\simeq B_S$ be the scalar tensor and unit comparisons, and write $u_R$ for the right unitor. The normalized adjunction states $\epsilon_{R,K}=u_R(1\otimes t_R)\pi_{R,K}^{-1}$. The new ordered projection square gives $F_B(a_K)\beta_q(G_AK)T_S(\pi_{A,K})=\pi_{B,X}(1_X\otimes b)m_{K,H_A}$. The normalized splitting gives $t_Bb=eT_S(t_A)$, with this very balanced $\lambda$.

proof.text:
Since $q$ is proper of finite type between Noetherian schemes and the rings are finite, the ordered projection maps are isomorphisms. Cancel them in the preceding square and substitute the actual counit formulas:
$$\begin{aligned}\epsilon_{B,X}F_B(a_K)\beta_q(G_AK)&=u_B(1_X\otimes t_Bb)m_{K,H_A}T_S(\pi_{A,K}^{-1})\\&=u_B(1_X\otimes e)(1_X\otimes T_St_A)m_{K,H_A}T_S(\pi_{A,K}^{-1})\\&=T_S\bigl(u_A(1_K\otimes t_A)\pi_{A,K}^{-1}\bigr)=T_S(\epsilon_{A,K}).\end{aligned}$$
The last equality uses tensorator naturality at $(1_K,t_A)$ and its right-unit equation $u_B(1_X\otimes e)m_{K,A_S}=T_S(u_A)$. Here $m$ and $e$ of def-pur-exceptional-coefficient-normalizations are, by its uniqueness clause, the tensor and unit comparisons $t_h,e_h$ of the ringed-topos pullback along $(S,B_S)\to(S,A_S)$ in the cited monoidal comparisons, since both are computed by ordinary balancing on K-flat representatives; so these two identities apply to them.

source.place: Charts: compatibility of iterated projective-line integration, actual counit at a complex; retained Step 7

proof.text: All comparisons are natural. The functors $F_R$, $G_R$, $T_S$ and $T_P$ preserve the $D^b_{ctf}$ subcategories, so both adjunctions $F_R\dashv G_R$ restrict to them and $\beta_q$ is invertible on all of $D^b_{ctf}(P_{et},A)$ by the proper coefficient theorem of step 1, so $\beta_q^{-1}$ is a natural transformation there. Compose the counit identity with $\beta_q(G_AK)^{-1}$. Under the actual exceptional adjunction $F_B\dashv G_B$, it says precisely that $a_K$ is the unique transpose of $T_S(\epsilon_{A,K})\circ\beta_q(G_AK)^{-1}$. The defining mate bijection therefore gives the final assertion.
